info.name: Sanad Admin — Chat reports
info.description: Support review of Chat reports (frozen contract endpoints 12-15): the report queue, report detail, the reported-conversation message view (the only non-participant read path in the chat slice), and dismiss/uphold. All routes sit behind the ChatSupportAdmin policy — login as a seeded SuperAdmin or SupportAdmin with normal access (see the Sanad.Admin collection folder 01 for login). Read-only with respect to conversation state, except uphold, which records the violation and applies a mutual chat-block in one save. Requests, bodies, and response examples are statically authored from the verified AdminChatReportsController/handler behavior and docs/chat/reports/lane-b-reports.md — they were never executed against a live API or database, and no secrets are stored here. Run only against disposable fixtures.

item.name: Queue — list reports (paged, optional status filter)

request.description: Endpoint 12 → 200 PagedResult {items, page, pageSize, totalCount, totalPages}, newest report first (createdOnUtc descending, id descending as tie-break). status is optional: blank/absent means no filter; otherwise Open, Dismissed, or Upheld, matched case-insensitively (a defined numeric enum value is also accepted). An unrecognised value is 400 Chat.Report.Invalid — a typo is never silently answered with an unfiltered page. page is clamped up to 1; pageSize is clamped to 1–100 (default 20). Each item is the full ReportResponse the detail view returns. Errors: 401 without a token; 403 for any authenticated account outside the ChatSupportAdmin policy (SuperAdmin + SupportAdmin, normal access).

request.description: Endpoint 13 → 200 with the full ReportResponse: stored fields (reportId, conversationId, optional messageId, reporterUserId, reason), the lifecycle status (Open/Dismissed/Upheld), and the resolution audit (resolvedOnUtc + resolvedBy = the acting admin's JWT user id) once Support closed it, null on both while Open. Support-only read — there is deliberately no participant check; the ChatSupportAdmin policy is the authorization. Unknown report id → plain 404 with code Chat.Report.NotFound (the admin route never privacy-forces: Support is never a participant, so the code survives for clients to key on). 401/403 as on the queue.

request.description: Endpoint 13 → 200 array of every message of the reported conversation, newest first, in the endpoint 3 item shape (id, conversationId, clientMessageId, senderUserId, type, text, attachment {attachmentId}, location, createdOnUtc, deliveredOnUtc, readOnUtc). The report id is the caller's entire authorization: this route is the ONLY non-participant read path in the chat slice, and Support has no general chat access. Read-only: unlike endpoint 3 this path never stamps deliveredOnUtc, never writes a read state, and never saves — Support observes, it does not participate. readOnUtc uses the participants' read rule with the reader fixed to whoever did not send the message, so the view never disagrees with what the participants saw. No cursor or filter — the whole conversation is returned. Unknown report id (or missing conversation integrity backstop) → plain 404 with code Chat.Report.NotFound. 401/403 as on the queue.

item.name: Dismiss report (close with history, no block)

request.description: Endpoint 14 → 204. Closes the report without action: status becomes Dismissed and the resolution stamps resolvedBy (admin JWT user id) plus resolvedOnUtc (server UTC). Nothing is erased — the reason, reporter, and conversation stay readable through the queue and detail, and no block is created. Only an Open report resolves; dismiss-after-dismiss, uphold-after-dismiss, and the reverse all answer 409 with code Chat.Report.InvalidState. Unknown report id → plain 404 (Chat.Report.NotFound). 401/403 as on the queue.

request.description: Endpoint 15 → 204. Records the violation (status Upheld + the same resolvedBy/resolvedOnUtc audit as dismiss) AND applies a mutual chat-block between the reported conversation's two participants: one block row per direction, created with the block endpoint's idempotent pre-check (a pre-existing row is left exactly as it is; the unique pair index is the backstop). Atomic: the Open-only guard runs before any block is created and everything lands in one save — a rejected re-uphold never leaves a partial block behind. Afterwards neither participant can send to the other; per the locked generic-failure rule each blocked sender receives the same indistinguishable privacy 404 as a non-participant (visible in each party's GET /api/v1/chat/blocks list; unblock removes one direction). Only an Open report resolves: a second resolve in either direction is 409 Chat.Report.InvalidState (and no block row is touched). Unknown report id → plain 404 (Chat.Report.NotFound). 401/403 as on the queue.
